propositions: Event bodies containing live credentials are accepted and written to disk with no content screening, allowing secrets to be published when the store auto-pushes to a shared branch

The store accept path is fragmented across append_event, txn/delete cores, and reconciler inbound translate, so a screen in one location bypasses others, leaving Jira-sourced external input unprotected

A single credential published in a comment triggered GitHub push protection rejection on refs/heads/tickets, queuing all concurrent sessions' writes local-only and wedging the entire store-sharing system for 153 commits

Detection must distinguish live credentials from benign descriptions (truncated placeholders, regex literals, prose enumerating banners), which appear with high false-positive density in the existing store
The refusal message and logs must not echo the secret value itself, even though the seam function has access to it, to prevent secondary leaks through logging or stderr during error handling
